Modern.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Norman Borlaug, agronomist whose dwarf wheat drove the Green Revolution and won the 1970 Nobel Peace Prize. Borlaug is the public-domain hero of high-yield breeding; pairing with 'Field' grounds it in the operating reality. Picked from A's three: cleanest anchor for a modern, data-forward voice.
Modern.industrySummary: AgTech in 2025 is consolidating around precision agronomy, on-farm sensing, and outcomes-based input contracts. Growers are tired of dashboards that don't change the planter pass. The market rewards firms that prove yield and margin uplift, not feature lists.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Indigo Ag (indigoag.com) leads on outcomes-based agronomy and carbon. Granular (granular.ag) holds the farm-management software middle. Farmers Business Network (fbn.com) is the buyer's-co-op modern reference. We sit closest to Indigo with a sharper breeding lens.
Modern.positioningStatement: Borlaug & Field is a data-forward agronomy partner for high-yield, climate-resilient row-crop operations.

Modern.tagline: Genetics for the next century of crops.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Nikolai Vavilov, Russian botanist who built the first seed bank in Leningrad in the 1920s and mapped the centers of crop origin. His staff starved during the WWII siege rather than eat the seed collection. Picked from A's three for the depth and morality of the anchor; reads as a serious breeding house.
Modern.industrySummary: Seed and trait genetics are the most leveraged input on a farm. Climate volatility has pushed growers toward diversified varietals and short-season backups, opening room for an independent breeding house.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Bayer Crop Science (cropscience.bayer.com) is the incumbent. Corteva (corteva.com) is the second major. Inari (inari.com) plays the modern gene-edit challenger. We sit closer to Inari, with a heritage-collection lineage.
Modern.positioningStatement: Vavilov Seedworks breeds and licenses climate-resilient, regionally adapted seed for independent growers and seed companies.

targetAudience.primary: Seed-company buyers, independent breeders, and large diversified farms.
behaviors: Field-trial across three regions before adoption

donts: Dress up commodity seed as breakthrough

typography.primary: Tiempos Headline for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne for body and trial data

Modern.tagline: What the soil is short of.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Justus von Liebig, the 19th-c German chemist who founded agricultural chemistry and the Law of the Minimum (yield is limited by the most-deficient nutrient). Picked from A's three for the clearest single-idea anchor — a soil lab can literally live the Law of the Minimum.
Modern.industrySummary: Soil testing and nutrient planning have moved from a once-a-decade chore to a season-by-season service, driven by fertilizer price volatility and runoff regulation. Independent soil labs that bundle sampling, lab work, and prescription writing are growing fast.
Modern.competitorLandscape: A&L Laboratories (allabs.com) holds the U.S. independent-lab middle. Ward Laboratories (wardlab.com) is the Plains-states reference. Yara (yara.com) leads on prescription nutrition globally. We sit closer to Ward with sharper analytics.
Modern.positioningStatement: Liebig Soil Lab is an independent soil-science lab that turns sample data into season-by-season nutrient prescriptions.

targetAudience.primary: Independent agronomists, mid-sized growers, and CCAs writing nutrient plans.

donts: Sell extra inputs the soil doesn't need
Use the word 'biological' as a slogan
